title: Execution of the Equality Program
statement: Let $P$ be a register program with oracle, let $r_1$ and $r_2$ be distinct registers, and let $e_C,e_{B_y},e_{B_n},y,n$ be states. Assume the transition function at these three states satisfies the specified equality-check and branching action rules, respectively, for every input symbol and tuple of scanned work-tape symbols, and assume the program makes no oracle call at any of these states. If registers $r_1,r_2$ initially store the buffer tapes for the binary words of natural numbers $a,b$, then there is a time $T$ at which execution from the configuration with state $e_C$ and both heads at cell $0$ reaches the same configuration with state $y$ when $a=b$ and state $n$ otherwise. At every earlier time $t<T$, the configuration has some state $s$, both heads at a common cell $q$, no oracle call is made at $s$, and $-1\le q\le \ell$, where $\ell$ is the length of the binary word for $a$.
hypotheses_covered: At state $e_C$, the transition function equals the specified equality-check action for all input symbols and scanned-symbol tuples.
At state $e_{B_y}$, the transition function equals the specified positive-branch action for all input symbols and scanned-symbol tuples.
At state $e_{B_n}$, the transition function equals the specified negative-branch action for all input symbols and scanned-symbol tuples.
There is no oracle call at states $e_C$, $e_{B_y}$, or $e_{B_n}$.
Register $r_1$ initially stores the buffer tape for the binary word of $a$.
Register $r_2$ initially stores the buffer tape for the binary word of $b$.
caveat: The action constructions named in the hypotheses are not defined in the supplied context, so their operational details cannot be rendered more explicitly.
